newsitem.title: INDIA: Mementos boost Indian sub-continent gold demand.
newsitem.headline: Mementos boost Indian sub-continent gold demand.

text.p: Indian businesses are using gold as a way of rewarding workers and boosting their business, adding to demand for the precious metal, dealers said on Monday.
They said demand for gold in India and neighbouring Pakistan, both celebrating 50 years of independence from British rule, is expected to be steady in the next few weeks.
"Companies are buying gold to make mementos to give them to their workers during the coming festivals," said a dealer. A four-month-long Hindu festival season starts later in August.
He said at least 10 companies bought up to 300 kgs of gold recently to make coins and mementos with their motif on one side and the image of a god or goddess on the other.
Analyst Madhusudan Daga said purchases of gold by companies were rising following a sharp dip in prices recently when they hit a low of 4,350 rupees per 10 grammes.
A luxury car maker promised to give a gold coin of 30 grammes to each buyer of its vehicles. A state lottery offered 500 grammes to one kg of gold as a prize for winners.
On Friday the state-owned MMTC Ltd released a gold medallion designed to mark 50 years of India's independence from colonial British rule.
While one side of the 10-gramme medallion has a special independence anniversary logo designed by the government, the other shows India's map along with MMTC's logo.
Dealers in Bombay said gold was being brought into India by expatriate Indians paying import duty and by smugglers responding to growing demand.
Customs officials at Bombay's international airport said they had seized 10 kgs of smuggled gold bars in one week early this month.
On the Bombay bullion market, standard gold gained 20 rupees to 4,520 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday.
"Festival demand has already begun and jewellers are buying gold to build stocks ahead of the festivals," said dealer Mahavir Shah.
In Pakistan's chief commercial city of Karachi, gold prices are expected to rise slightly this week on fresh demand because of the current low prices, dealers said.

"Gold prices are down and these are good levels to buy," dealer M.S. Imran said. "The gold prices have gained in the international market and would also rise slightly in the domestic market on fresh demand."
Gold traders in Dubai, the business hub of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), said they expected demand to rise in the next week after the national holidays are over in the Indian sub-continent.

A Dubai-based refinery said it had doubled its output this month of the benchmark Ten Tola Bar (TT) to meet the expected rise in demand ahead of the festival season in India, the world's largest consumer of gold.
